look_here_first: Start with the narrow leaves and the stem hairs. Prairie spiderwort has narrow linear to strap-shaped leaves and conspicuous long-stalked glandular hairs on the internodes and peduncles. In the Williamson treatment the blades are about 6–17 mm wide, giving the plant a noticeably grassier look than giant spiderwort.

lookalikes.differences: T. gigantea is broader and more robust with a nearly glabrous lower stem. T. humilis is shorter, bushier and hairy across the vegetative plant. T. ohiensis is much more glabrous/glaucous in the upper stem and sepals; T. occidentalis has conspicuous glandular pubescence.
